messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gpu-pool-prod-usw2 capacity breach. queue_length=912, inflight_tokens=1.2M, autoscaler_error=ScaleLimitReached. Paging oncall: @emma

emma: Got the page. Looking at graphs now. Any customer reports yet?

support-liaison: Yes — two enterprise customers reported 503s and heavy throttling for embeddings since ~03:02. CS is triaging with them.

maria: I'm seeing steady queue growth on the embeddings route. Pod pending count spiked; kube-autoscaler attempted 4 scale ops and hit account-level GPU limit. Also seeing a lot of partially utilized nodes — MIG fragmentation.

raj: Key datapoints I see: autoscaler logs show failures: "cannot allocate GPUs: no binpack fit for requested migProfile". We have many nodes with leftover 1/2 MIG slices but requests need 1 full GPU or specific MIG size. Binpacking + strict mig profiles = stranded capacity.

emma: So autoscaler didn't add because account limit hit, and scheduling can't fill fragments. What's faster: bump limits or change scheduling constraints?

ken: Bumping cloud quota will take ~20-40m. We can do two immediate things: 1) enable fallback to lower-gpu-profile models for non-SLA customers, 2) temporarily relax mig_profile constraints so scheduler can place into smaller slices. Both need infra change.

maria: I can push a runtime config to allow MIG-size downgrades for new pods (flag: runtime.allow_mig_overprovision=true). That will let scheduler accept 1/2 MIG allocation. But existing pinned requests will still be stuck.

emma: Do the runtime change. raj, can you try a manual scale override for the prod pool to add +3 nodes (force) while we request quota? Command I want: 

raj: Running: 
```
# manual emergency increase
infractl pools scale --region us-west-2 --pool gpu-prod --add 3 --force --reason "incident 1781008245 emergency"
```

deploy-bot: infractl: scale request submitted (req-5542). Provisioning nodes (expected ~6m).

maria: Pushed runtime flag. Rolling create for pods will start accepting 1/2-MIG. Need to drain a few older pods to consolidate.

ken: Also toggled routing: embeddings requests for non-enterprise tenants now go to hosted-fallback to reduce pressure. Command: `routectl set-route embeddings --fallback hosted-fallback --percentage 40`

support-liaison: Noted. CS updated the impacted customers and offered incident updates. One customer requested ETA; they are sensitive to SLO violations.

emma: We're seeing queue length stabilize from 912 -> 720 after routing change. But throttling still happening for enterprise tenants.

raj: New problem: some nodes are showing MIG slices that can't be combined because of pinned driver versions and older kubelet ephemeral mapping. I can try a rolling reboot on a subset to let the node reclaim GPUs. Will do a small window to avoid more pod churn.

maria: Reboots may evict pods; we need to ensure autoscaler doesn't kill additional capacity. I'll annotate nodes with `no-scale-down` during reboots.

raj: Executing rolling reboot on nodes: gpu-node-12, gpu-node-15, gpu-node-19 (3 at a time).

emma: Handing over to raj for 03:30–04:00 watch. I'll take customer comms and write an interim incident update. If anything critical happens ping @emma.

raj: Confirming takeover. Watching queue and scheduler events. Reboots started.

(3m later)
raj: Reboot round 1 complete. Kube reports reclaimed 2 full GPUs from fragmented nodes. Scheduler placed 14 pending pods. queue_length -> 430.

maria: Autoscaler req-5542 finished; 3 new nodes provisioned. However, one node failed healthcheck (driver mismatch) and is in NotReady. I'm isolating it.

emma: Customer-impact note: Enterprise customers A and B saw median latency spikes 8x; errors peaked ~03:10–03:20. CS sent targeted updates, offered credits.

ken: Quota request submitted to cloud support with high priority. ETA unknown. If quota comes in we can scale further.

raj: After reboots + runtime flag, pending queue drained to ~120. Most enterprise requests now hitting fallback model (smaller instance) or being placed. We still have ~40 requests stuck that require specific MIG profile (1g-16gb).

maria: Those 40 are long-lived chat sessions pinned to a 1g MIG. We can evict low-priority ones — any objections?

emma: Approve evict for low-priority sessions. Notify customers if session will be interrupted.

support-liaison: Sending notifications now.

(another 12m)
raj: Final note: autoscaler config had two issues: 1) scaleLimitPerRegion set too low after last deploy (accidentally 12 instead of 32), 2) strict_mig_profile_enforcement defaulted true after release. I've opened a PR to revert defaults and added guarded feature flags.

maria: Confirmed: after we evicted low-priority sessions and node reboots, stranded GPU slices reduced by ~70% and queue drained to <10. Error rates back to baseline.

emma: Declaring incident mitigated at 04:23. Root cause summary: quota + autoscaler scale limit + MIG binpacking mismatch leading to stranded capacity. Immediate mitigations: manual scale (+3), runtime flag to relax MIG constraints, rolling node reboots, routing fallback for non-SLA tenants, customer comms.

emma: Postmortem owner: raj. Action items assigned: 
- raj: PR to fix autoscaler defaults + add alert for low regional scaleLimit (due in 72h)
- maria: automated repair job to detect MIG fragmentation and trigger consolidation (due 7d)
- ken: follow up with cloud support to raise quota and validate limits (due 24h)
- support-liaison: consolidate customer messages and follow-up credits for impacted customers (due 48h)

emma: I'll leave the thread open for any follow-ups. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:
